biodiversity_overview.text: 1,015 GBIF occurrence records for 32 tracked species are attributed to Meghalaya, spanning 1915-2026.
973 of these records (95.9%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 12, Mammalia 10, Magnoliopsida 5, Actinopterygii 3, Squamata 1, Testudines 1.

threatened_species.text: 2 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
1 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Asian Elephant (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian White-eye (519), Indian Cuckoo (196), Indian Gooseberry (98), Indian Pied Starling (60), Mango (22).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 33 in 2016 to 4 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 2.03% of Meghalaya's area (8 areas intersect the state).
1.0% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (10 of 973); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Peacock Soft-shelled Turtle (0.50), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), African Mottled Eel (0.43), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Indian Grass-babbler (0.30).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Meghalaya (equal-weight reference): cell near 25.875N 90.375E (overall rank 189, median rank across weightings 194); cell near 25.125N 91.875E (overall rank 217, median rank across weightings 238); cell near 25.125N 90.375E (overall rank 369, median rank across weightings 366).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 16,877 km2 (71.99% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

2,450.0 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (14.52% of the 2000 extent; 9.05% in 2015-2024, rank 5 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2017 (235.61 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.56% of land and population density is 207.2 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
17% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
